review.tagline: Long-term memory store for coding agents, with sources and corrections
review.summary: GBrain keeps explicit facts and their sources in a local PGLite or Postgres brain and exposes them to agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Hermes over stdio or HTTP MCP. It starts keyless with keyword search; semantic search, cited synthesis, a typed knowledge graph and an overnight enrichment cycle are optional. It is installed with Bun from GitHub, not npm.
review.audience: Developers giving Claude Code, Codex or other agents persistent shared memory
strengths: Keyless start: PGLite brain with keyword search, no server or Docker needed
One brain shared across agents via stdio MCP or HTTP MCP with scoped OAuth tokens
One-command setup for Claude Code and Codex, with dry-run and remove options
Optional cited synthesis that notes gaps, plus a typed graph for relationship queries
weaknesses: Not on npm; the unrelated npm package named gbrain can shadow the real binary
Always-on OpenClaw/Hermes setup needs a server with 8GB+ RAM plus paid API usage
Local files and shared database credentials are not isolated by sources
Remote put_page does not extract graph edges inline; HTTP needs explicit maintenance
needs: Needs Bun 1.4.0+, PGLite or Postgres, Tailscale (optional, for remote MCP)
Models: Optional cloud embedding, reranking, extraction and synthesis providers (unspecified)
